finding_label: Dietary responses separate processing potential from immune outcomes
finding_summary: Human dietary intervention can change processing potential without increased diversity; immune responses require separate interpretation.
finding_interpretation: The prespecified cytokine-response score did not change. Gene abundance is functional potential, not enzyme flux; stool metabolite concentration is not production rate. Diversity and immune changes were accompanying results, not demonstrated causal mediation. No improvement in cognition surveys, glucose, lipids or blood pressure was established.
finding_statement: High-fibre intake can increase metagenomic glycan-processing potential without increased diversity, while fermented-food-associated immune changes do not establish diversity-mediated benefit.
synthesis: In Wastyk et al., 18 healthy adults were analysed in each free-living dietary arm after a four-week ramp and six-week maintenance. Fibre increased from 21.5 to 45.1 g/day; glycan-degrading CAZyme gene abundance increased with stable diversity. Residual stool carbohydrate increased with fibre intake, leaving processing sufficiency unresolved. Fermented foods increased from 0.4 to 6.3 servings/day; diversity increased and 19 of 93 circulating inflammatory proteins decreased, including IL-6, IL-10 and IL-12b.
synthesis_limitations: The prespecified cytokine-response score did not change. Gene abundance is functional potential, not enzyme flux; stool metabolite concentration is not production rate. Diversity and immune changes were accompanying results, not demonstrated causal mediation. No improvement in cognition surveys, glucose, lipids or blood pressure was established.

evidence_considered.label: Wastyk et al. (2021)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Fibre changed CAZyme potential without increased diversity; fermented foods changed diversity and inflammatory proteins without establishing mediation.

assessment.study: Free-living dietary trial; Figure 3C–E, Figures 5–6 and primary-outcome methods/Table S4
assessment.population: 18 healthy adults analysed per arm; high-fibre versus high-fermented-food dietary exposure
assessment.result: Distinct community-capacity and immune responses occurred across the two arms.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Fibre 21.5→45.1 g/day; fermented foods 0.4→6.3 servings/day; 19/93 inflammatory proteins decreased in that arm.
assessment.evidence_summary: Preserves the measured inflammatory response without attributing it to diversity or a defined taxon.
assessment.limitations: No untreated control arm or diversity-mediation test; primary cytokine-response score unchanged; potential, activity and host outcomes remain distinct.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Schleupner and Carmichael (2022)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Review is not an experiment establishing competitive selection or benefit from increased diversity.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Prehn-Kristensen et al. (2018)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Does not measure dietary selection, turnover or processing activity.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Steckler et al. (2024)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Case–control stool composition and SCFA concentrations.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Concentration is not production flux; specific SCFA claims belong to PM5 and no dietary modifiability is established.
